question: How could lamb shipped from New Zealand to Britain carry a smaller carbon footprint than lamb raised in Britain?
answer: Because the farm matters more than the ship. A 2006 Lincoln University study found New Zealand lamb, raised on year-round pasture with little fertiliser or bought feed, emitted about a quarter of the carbon dioxide per tonne of British lamb, shipping included. The study came from New Zealand, and such comparisons are contested.
move: Distance is one cost among many; ask which one is largest.
ask: Where am I judging something by how far it travelled instead of how it was made?
reference: Saunders, Barber & Taylor, Food Miles – Comparative Energy/Emissions Performance of New Zealand's Agriculture Industry, AERU Research Report 285, Lincoln University, 2006
